Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Summit Insurance Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Summit Insurance Group's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Underwriting Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Summit Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by robust net written premiums growth across personal, commercial, specialty, and life & health lines, disciplined underwriting that kept our ex-cat combined ratio in the low 90s, resilient catastrophe loss management despite elevated events, and a progressive dividend policy underscoring our capital return strength.

Michael, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Rivera: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $285 million, or $1.12 adjusted operating earnings per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included strong top-line expansion from net written premiums, meaningful investment income growth, and underwriting excellence amid a challenging catastrophe environment. Our combined ratio was 96.8%, reflecting effective underwriting and claims management. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with our consolidated RBC ratio at 580%, well above our 450% target.

Let me start by providing an update on our dividend policy, which remains a cornerstone of our capital return framework and a testament to our disciplined underwriting and investment discipline. For the quarter ended September 30, 2024, our Board of Directors has declared a quarterly common stock dividend of $0.48 per share, payable on November 15th to shareholders of record as of October 25th. This represents a 6.7% increase from the $0.45 per share paid in Q3 2023 and a 2.1% sequential increase from our Q2 2024 payout of $0.47. On a trailing twelve-month basis, this brings our annualized dividend to $1.92 per share, up from $1.80 in 2023—a 6.7% year-over-year growth that aligns with our target of mid-single-digit annual increases, supported by compounding earnings power.

To put this in context, our dividend has grown at a robust 5.2% compound annual growth rate over the past five years, outpacing the S&P 500 Insurance Index average of 4.1%. This track record reflects our consistent ability to generate free cash flow from operations—$1.2 billion in the first nine months of 2024 alone—while maintaining a prudent payout ratio of 44% of adjusted operating EPS. Our Q3 adjusted operating EPS came in at $1.12 per share, up 8% year-over-year, providing more than 2.4x coverage for the quarterly dividend. Even on a GAAP basis, including some $150 million in elevated catastrophe losses from recent hurricanes and wildfires, our coverage remains solid at over 1.8x.

Driving this sustainability are several key trends and strategic levers unique to our industry positioning. Our consolidated ex-cat combined ratio improved to 92.8% in Q3, down 110 basis points year-over-year, thanks to rate adequacy across our property & casualty book—up an average 9.2% on renewals—and loss ratio mitigation from our proprietary telematics platform in personal auto, now covering 65% of policies. This mirrors what peers like Progressive and Travelers have achieved through data-driven pricing amid softening market conditions.

Investment income provided tailwinds as well, with our $45 billion general account portfolio yielding 3.8% in Q3, boosted by higher reinvestment rates in investment-grade municipals and corporates, duration steady at 5.9 years. Fixed income now comprises 78% of the portfolio, with unrealized losses narrowing to just 2.1% of amortized cost following Fed pivot expectations. This generated $420 million in net investment income, up 12% year-over-year, directly fueling distributable earnings.

Regionally, in the U.S., our core P&C segment—representing 55% of net premiums earned—delivered $2.8 billion in NPE growth, with commercial lines up 11% on strong workers' comp and excess & surplus demand. Cat losses totaled $220 million pre-tax, but our quota-share reinsurance tower caps our net retention at 40%, preserving capital. Europe saw 7% NPE growth in our Lloyd’s syndicate and direct operations, aided by favorable motor rate increases amid inflation, though we’re monitoring French flood risks. Asia-Pacific, now 18% of NPE via our joint ventures with partners like Manulife, grew 15% in life & health, driven by embedded value release from unit-linked products in Singapore and India. This diversification offsets U.S. cat volatility.

Strategically, we’re enhancing dividend capacity through targeted initiatives. Our 'InsureTech 2.0' platform, leveraging AI for straight-through claims processing now at 72% automation rate, shaved our expense ratio by 80 basis points to 28.5%, unlocking $180 million in annual savings. We’ve also optimized our reinsurance program with a new $1.5 billion catastrophe aggregate cover from Swiss Re and RenaissanceRe, reducing tail risk by 25%. On the capital front, this allows $500 million in share repurchases YTD alongside dividends, trading at 1.4x book value.

Looking ahead, we reaffirm our commitment to progressive dividend growth, targeting 5-7% annual increases through the cycle, contingent on sustained ROE above 12%, currently at 13.8% trailing. In a hardening reinsurance market and with interest rates stabilizing, we see ample room to compound per-share value, much like Berkshire’s insurance operations or Chubb’s playbook. This balanced approach—dividends plus buybacks—has delivered 18% total shareholder return over three years, outperforming the KBW Property Casualty Index by 500 basis points.

Turning now to our top-line performance, specifically net written premiums, or NWP, which grew 8.7% year-over-year to $14.2 billion. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-cat growth and reflects disciplined underwriting, favorable rate momentum, and strong retention across the portfolio. Excluding the impacts of foreign exchange and our recent acquisition of Midwest Specialty Risk, organic NWP growth came in at a robust 7.2%, ahead of our guided 6-8% full-year range.

Breaking this down by line of business highlights the health of our book amid elevated catastrophe activity like Hurricane Beryl and California wildfires, plus persistent inflation on repair and medical costs. Personal lines led with 11.4% NWP growth to $6.8 billion, driven by a 9% increase in policies in-force and average rate hikes of 7.2% net of competition. Auto surged 12.8% to $4.1 billion, fueled by our ApexDrive telematics program, now at 28% penetration—up from 22% last year. This usage-based model improves risk selection, with telematics-insured drivers showing 15% lower loss ratios, attracting millennials and gig workers. Homeowners grew 9.2% to $2.7 billion, with 6.5% rate increases pricing for 4-5% annual inflation in materials like lumber and labor. Retention held at 88%. U.S. personal lines grew 12.1%, led by Florida and Texas post-Ian, while our European book, 15% of the segment, expanded 6% despite UK regulatory caps.

Commercial lines saw 6.9% NWP growth to $4.9 billion, with rates up 5.8% overall—softening in middle-market but firm in excess & surplus. Workers' comp led at 8.2% to $1.8 billion, thanks to 4% payroll growth and our AI-powered ApexPredict tool analyzing OSHA data to shave 2 points off loss picks. General liability and property each grew 6.5%, focused on preferred non-cat risks. New business rose 7.1%, with retention at 87% via account-based servicing and cyber bundling. U.S. commercial up 7.5%, strong post-Midwest acquisition; EMEA up 3% despite German rate erosion.

Specialty lines accelerated with 15.2% NWP growth to $2.1 billion, now 15% of our book after doubling over three years. Cyber exploded 22% to $850 million amid 30% ransomware rise per Chainalysis; our parametric product covers 40% of writings for faster payouts. D&O grew 14% with 9% rates on ESG litigation fears. Trade credit and marine added 12%, with blockchain tracking cutting fraud 18%. Asia-Pacific specialty jumped 18% via Singapore and Australia partnerships with Swiss Re.

Life & health grew 4.2% to $400 million on 3% group health renewals combating 7.5% medical trends, piloting embedded insurance like Sun Life.

Pricing drove 5.5 points of growth, volume 2.8 points, retention/mix 0.4 points. Book yield rose 6.2%, supporting mid-90s combined ratios despite $1.2 billion cats. We've invested $150 million in gen AI for pricing, dynamically adjusting loss trends. Regionally: U.S. +10.2% (65%), EMEA +4.8% (20%), Asia-Pac +12% (10%), LatAm +7% (5%). We're non-renewing 15% Florida homeowners, redirecting to cyber/parametrics. FY24 NWP outlook 8-9%, specialty 18-20%, with tech distribution and M&A like Midwest.

Before we move on, a deeper look at total catastrophe losses, net of reinsurance recoveries, which came in at $1.42 billion pre-tax for Q3, or 4.8% of our quarterly GWP of $29.6 billion. This compares to $850 million or 3.1% in Q3 2023, and $620 million or 2.2% in Q2 2024. Year-to-date, $2.85 billion or 3.2% of YTD GWP of $89.2 billion—up 36% from full-year 2022.

By region and event: U.S. (65%, $920 million) from Hurricane Elena's Category 3 landfall in Florida Panhandle, net after multi-layer treaties; plus $180 million California wildfires, up 25% from drought. Europe (22%, $310 million) from Storm Boris floods in Germany/Poland, 5.1% of GWP. Asia-Pacific (10%, $140 million) Typhoon Kiko in Japan/Philippines, 3.4%. Other 3% ($50 million) hail in Australia. These added 320 bps to our 98.4% accident year combined ratio; ex-cat loss ratio improved 50 bps to 61.2% on 9.2% U.S. personal renewals.

Mitigation via ZenCat model with ML for windfields, reducing Florida exposure 12%; ceded 55% via $2 billion XSOL with Swiss Re, $450 million Q3 recoveries. Diversifying: trimmed California 15%, grew EMEA non-flood 22%; cat deductibles up 18%, parametric wildfires; 2024 reinsurance 7% cheaper; $500 million cat bond at 4.75%. FY24 cat guide $3.4-3.8 billion or 3.5-4.0% GWP, per Verisk $85 billion industry.

On combined ratio performance and forward guidance: Q3 ex-cat at 91.2%, all-in 96.8% after $185 million cats from Hurricane Helene and European windstorms—11th straight sub-97% ex-cat quarter. Loss ratio aided by 2 points PYD ($48 million) in workers' comp/D&O. Expense ratio 30.4%, efficiencies from Guidewire Cloud at 85% rollout, 92% straight-through processing.

Guidance: FY24 ex-cat 93.5-94.5%, all-in 96.0-97.5% with $650-700 million cats, Q4-weighted on La Niña storms. Q4 ex-cat 92.0-93.5%, all-in 95.0-97.0% assuming $200-250 million cats (8-10 points), per RMS v18.

Assumptions: rates 11.5% commercial/9.2% auto >6-7% trends; U.S. P&C (65%) sub-92% ex-cat on 45% telematics; Europe 98-100% all-in mitigated by Munich Re; Asia sub-90% parametrics up 22%. AI underwriting with Cytora/Duck Creek cuts manual work 35% for climate risks; reinsurance 5% cheaper on $1.2 billion program. Risks: cat upside, medical inflation; see 92% ex-cat 2025 for 10-12% ROE.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from David Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Chen: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the sustainability of your dividend increases given the cat pressures?

Michael Rivera: Good morning, David. Absolutely, our dividend sustainability is rock-solid, with 2.4x coverage on adjusted EPS and strong free cash flow generation. The 5.2% five-year CAGR outpaces peers, backed by underwriting discipline—ex-cat 92.8%—and investment yields at 3.8%. Our RBC at 580% and reinsurance optimizations give us flexibility for 5-7% annual growth, as we've executed with buybacks too.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of elevated cat activity and La Niña on your combined ratio guidance?

Elena Vasquez: Good morning, Lisa. Cats at 4.8% of GWP this quarter were elevated, but our modeling and reinsurance—55% ceded—kept net impact manageable. Guidance embeds $650-700 million FY cats, Q4 at 8-10 points, with ex-cat holding 92-93.5% on rate adequacy outpacing trends and telematics gains. La Niña boosts storm risk, but diversification and parametrics position us well for sub-97% all-in.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Kline with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline: Thanks. On NWP growth, how sustainable is the specialty lines acceleration, especially cyber?

Johnathan Hale: Robert, specialty at 15.2% growth is strategic, cyber up 22% on ransomware demand. Parametrics and blockchain fraud reduction enable margins, with Asia up 18%. We'll target 18-20% in FY24, offsetting any auto softening via tech distribution and M&A.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Torres with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Torres: Good morning. Any updates on regional cat exposures post-Elena?

Michael Rivera: Emily, post-Elena, we've proactively trimmed Florida coastal by 12% via non-renewals and rates. U.S. net $920 million, but quota shares cap retention. Europe floods mitigated by models, Asia in line. Long-term, targeting under 3% GWP nat cat load through diversification.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] That concludes our Q&A session.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Summit Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
